reproduction_notes:
# Fast Node / BinaryTrie measurements

The benchmark sources are shared by baseline, byte-identical control, and Fast. They use the same API sequence, generated inputs, compiler flags, executable path, and SKIP_RUNTIME_CHECKS setting. Node differs only in the required handle representation (`shared_ptr<Node>` versus `Node*`) and conversion to a non-owning pointer for checks. Source snapshots and hashes are in `freeze.json`.

Build and correctness work runs on logical CPU0. Performance execution is pinned to logical CPU12, a P-Core of the i9-14900K. Each case has seven outer repetitions in a shuffled variant order. `bench_clock.hpp` records both steady-clock wall time and CLOCK_THREAD_CPUTIME_ID to diagnose preemption. Stopwatch reads are outside the repeated API loops; durations near the timer cost must not be interpreted as precise per-object nanoseconds.

Each process separately records construction, the operation loop, and destruction. Construction includes ordinary wrapper/handle storage and, for read/delete cases of BinaryTrie, the documented prefill. The sum of these three phases is a library-lifecycle measurement. It is not total application exit time: OS reclamation of retained Fast storage happens after the final timestamp. `process_elapsed_ns` includes input generation, correctness checks, startup and exit, and is only a diagnostic.

Node cases: size, tail, indexed traversal, reversal, cycle test, clone, push+pop, explicit clear, and creating/breaking a cycle. Sizes range from zero to one million. Clone stores outputs until the separately timed destruction phase. For push+pop, ordinary deallocation during pop is part of that API operation. Checks and identity/order verification are outside the operation timer.

BinaryTrie cases: anonymous/ID insertion and deletion, count+contains, rank/count_less, min/max XOR with lazy XOR, repeated ID-slot reuse in a 16-key domain, and a deterministic mixed operation stream. It uses uint32_t keys with 30 bits and NODES=67108864, comfortably above the ordinary virtual-node and Fast physical-node requirements in these inputs. Read/delete cases prefill the same values during construction. A whole process is used per variant so intentional retained storage does not contaminate later repetitions.

Memory observations are a separate instrumented run, not a speed measurement. A global allocation wrapper counts dynamically requested bytes/calls and frees; its header overhead is excluded from `live_requested_bytes`. Stack object storage is also excluded. maxrss is a Linux high-water diagnostic, not an exact live-memory measure. Lifecycles and repeated ID reuse show which allocations remain after clear/destruction and which capacities stabilize.

Fast intentionally omits reclamation. LeakSanitizer is disabled for its tests; ASan, UBSan and libstdc++ vector poisoning remain enabled. Correctness tests use only the valid-input contracts. Node has independent vector/function-graph/visited-node/Floyd models, acyclic and cyclic graphs, aliases, reversals and million-node chains. BinaryTrie combines the existing normal/reference map fixture with a separate full-width/small-width/ID/XOR/rank fixture. No claim is made about exception recovery, invalid inputs, exhausted capacity or interoperability between ordinary and raw Node ownership types.

The initial Node-only measurements in `measurements/` used only a boolean from tail/index queries and exposed an optimizer artifact: Clang could remove raw tail traversal and raw push/pop allocation. Those Node results are excluded as speed evidence. The corrected `node_bench.cpp` uses the same opaque pointer/memory escape for all variants, including the newly created head before pop. The remeasurements live in `measurements_node_escape/` and add the frozen `pool_node.hpp` candidate. BinaryTrie initial measurements remain valid and are kept separately.
